questions.subject: Reading
questions.learningObjective: Infer purpose and identify actions or conditions in everyday communications.
questions.passage: Lockers beside the library entrance are normally cleared at closing time. During exam week, students may leave books in a locker overnight if they collect a blue tag from the front desk before 6 p.m. Bags and electronics must still be taken home. Put the tag on the outside of the locker so that the evening staff can see it.
questions.prompt: What does the notice mainly announce?
questions.answer: A temporary exception to a locker rule.
questions.explanation: The overnight exception applies to books during exam week if the student obtains and displays a tag.
options: A change to the library's closing time.
A different location for the front desk.
A temporary exception to a locker rule.
A new service for charging electronics.

questions.prompt: Which student has followed the instructions?
questions.answer: One who gets a tag at 5 p.m., displays it and leaves only textbooks.
questions.explanation: The student meets the deadline, makes the tag visible and stores only books.
options: One who gets a tag at 5 p.m., displays it and leaves only textbooks.
One who leaves a laptop inside a tagged locker.
One who puts a tag inside the locker with the books.
One who arrives at 7 p.m. to request a tag.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.learningObjective: Infer purpose and identify actions or conditions in everyday communications.
questions.passage: Hi Tunde, thanks for offering to help at Saturday's seed swap. We've already filled all the slots at the welcome table, but could you make signs for the seed trays? If you can send the files by Thursday afternoon, we'll print them here. Otherwise, you can bring printed signs on Saturday. I’ve attached last year's signs so you can see the size we need. — Ada
questions.prompt: Why did Ada attach last year's signs?
questions.answer: To show Tunde what dimensions to use.
questions.explanation: Ada refers to the old signs as examples of the required size.
options: To show what seeds will arrive this year.
To give Tunde a list of table volunteers.
To ask Tunde to bring the old signs back.
To show Tunde what dimensions to use.

questions.prompt: What should Tunde do if the files will be ready only on Friday?
questions.answer: Print the signs and bring them to the swap.
questions.explanation: When the Thursday deadline cannot be met, Ada offers the option of bringing printed signs on Saturday.
options: Send the files and ask the garden team to print them.
Print the signs and bring them to the swap.
Ask for a shift at the welcome table instead.
Post the files for visitors to print.

questions.learningObjective: Infer purpose and identify actions or conditions in everyday communications.
questions.passage:
Lola: My meal order says pickup at the kiosk, but the kiosk is dark.
Staff: If your receipt says “ready,” use the side window. We are keeping the kiosk closed today because of the rain.
Lola: Mine still says “preparing.” Should I wait at the window?
Staff: There’s no need to queue yet. The order page will update when you can collect it.
questions.prompt: What does the staff member imply about Lola's order?
questions.answer: It will still be available for pickup when it is ready.
questions.explanation: The reply says the page will update when collection is possible.
options: It must be placed again at the side window.
It will be cancelled because of the rain.
It will still be available for pickup when it is ready.
It has already been handed to someone else.

questions.subject: Reading
questions.learningObjective: Infer purpose and identify actions or conditions in everyday communications.
questions.passage: Study rooms can be reserved for groups of two to six. Each reservation has a ten-minute grace period. After that, a room may be given to another group unless at least one member has checked in at the desk. To extend a reservation, look at the booking calendar while you are still in the room. An extension is possible only when the next slot is free.
questions.prompt: What can keep a reservation in place if some members are late?
questions.answer: One group member checks in within the grace period.
questions.explanation: A timely check-in by one member is sufficient under the stated rule.
options: One group member checks in within the grace period.
Everyone waits outside the room until the group is complete.
The group reserves the next slot in a different room.
A group member checks the calendar without visiting the desk.

An extension is possible only when the next slot is free.
questions.prompt: Why should a group check the booking calendar before asking for more time?
questions.answer: The calendar shows whether there is another reservation immediately after theirs.
questions.explanation: The next slot must be unreserved for the group to extend its stay.
options: The calendar shows how many people have checked in.
The calendar lists rooms that have no grace period.
The calendar gives desk opening hours for the next day.
The calendar shows whether there is another reservation immediately after theirs.

questions.passage: Bring a small item you would like to fix to the repair café. A volunteer will show you how to inspect it and, if possible, work through a repair with you. We have common hand tools. If you already know a replacement part is needed, bring it along. Please stay with your item during the session so you can practise the steps yourself.
questions.prompt: What is the flyer mainly promoting?
questions.answer: A hands-on session where people learn to repair their own items.
questions.explanation: Visitors stay and practise repair steps with a volunteer.
options: A drop-off counter offering repairs while customers are away.
A hands-on session where people learn to repair their own items.
A competition for people who already repair items professionally.
A shop that supplies specialist replacement parts.

questions.passage: The first riverbank count of the season is on Sunday. New volunteers should watch the short counting demonstration posted on the project page before signing up. Returning volunteers can sign up straight away. Choose either the early or the late slot. If the river path is closed after heavy rain, we will move the activity to the park and update the meeting point on the project page by Saturday evening.
questions.prompt: What must a first-time volunteer do before choosing a slot?
questions.explanation: The notice places the demonstration before registration for new volunteers.
options: Watch the project's counting demonstration.
Visit the park to check the meeting point.
Attend a riverbank count as an observer.
Ask a returning volunteer to make the booking.
